smoke.line: You creep toward the smoke. A small camp resolves out of the mist — a single firepit, a tarpaulin lean-to, a figure crouched over the coals.
smoke.arbiterLine: "Approach openly or not at all," the {narrator} says quietly. "This one is watching the road."

smoke.line: The figure looks up. A scavenger, mud to the knees, pack half-emptied. They wave you in. "Sit. Trade if you want. I have heard of a hollow two ridges over — old old work, no constructs."

effects.text: A Reclaimer at a roadside fire spoke of an unmapped hollow two ridges over.

vendor.name: Roadfire Reclaimer
vendor.title: Trader on the road
vendor.description: Sits the fire low, doesn't look up much. Holds out what they have one item at a time.

smoke.line: You and the scavenger part ways. They press a few coins into your palm "for the directions, when you find what is left of the place."

footprints.line: You follow the boot prints. They keep a steady stride, then bunch — someone stopped here. The trail veers behind a fallen column.
Behind the column, a body. Scavenger kit, cold for days. Their pack is mostly intact.
footprints.arbiterLine: "Tartaria takes them like this," the {narrator} says. "No drama. Just the next set of tracks that stop."

effects.text: You found a dead Reclaimer at the end of a track. Their compass now points for you.

obelisk.line: You crouch beside the stone. The runes are old old — half-faded, but readable if you trace them. A coiled glyph in the centre still throws a faint glow when your hand passes over it.
You press your palm to the glyph. A shock runs up your arm — not painful, just decisive. The stone has marked you.
obelisk.arbiterLine: "That is older than the Mud Monarchs," the {narrator} murmurs. "It will know you again."

effects.text: A Tartarian rune marked you. The True Tartarians will know.

wagon.line: You climb onto the broken axle. The wagon bed is half-emptied but the lockbox under the driver's bench is still sealed.
The lockbox cracks open. Inside — a smaller pouch of coin, a wrapped bundle of cloth, and a faintly humming shard.

arch.line: You duck under the half-buried arch. The passage opens into a hollow — an old work-room, equipment long since hauled away, but the walls still hum.
Set into the back wall, behind a curtain of dried mud, you find a small cache. Whoever told you of this place was telling the truth.
arch.arbiterLine: "This is what they sell information for," the {narrator} says.

effects.text: You found the hollow the Reclaimer described. The information was good.

glint.line: You pick the metal out of the rubble. A pendant — old make, hammered thin, etched with a faction crest.
You turn the pendant over. Whoever wore it last bled out clutching it — a faint rust-brown line still runs along the inside of the chain.
glint.arbiterLine: "That crest is the Forgotten Order's," the {narrator} says. "Carry it to their people and lay it down. They honor the ones who bring their dead home."

effects.text: A bloodstained Forgotten Order sigil — return it to their stake to honor their dead.

handprint.line: You crouch beside the print. Pressed deep — someone heavier than you, and recent. The dust around it has not yet settled.
You follow the prints to a low ridge. A True old scout, hooded and watching, dips their head once when you crest the hill — acknowledgement, not greeting — and is gone before you reach the ground.

effects.text: A True Tartarian scout marked you and let you pass. They are aware of you now.

thread.line: You pull the rubble aside. A draft of cold, old air, and a tight passage angling down into the dark.
You wedge yourself into the gap. At the bottom — a small antechamber, half-flooded, with three sealed jars on a shelf. You take what you can carry.

resonance.line: You step toward the pulse. The air thickens. The hum syncs with your heartbeat for a half-second, then drops away.
A shape unfolds itself out of the haze — something the size of a person, made of nothing the eye can hold. It moves toward you.
resonance.arbiterLine: "This is what comes of pulling at threads," the {narrator} says. "Do not pull lightly."

half_buried_spire.line: You cross the broken ground toward the spire. The bottom storeys are hardened glassed shut, but a window two heights up gapes open. A coil of old rope tells you someone else has tried.
You haul yourself through the window. Inside: a hall once-rich, now stripped, the strange grid in the walls still warm to the touch.
half_buried_spire.arbiterLine: "This was a noble house," the {narrator} says. "Mud Monarch stock. Take what is here before its owners remember to come back."

half_buried_spire.line: On the upper floor — a cabinet wedged behind a fallen beam. Coin and an unfamiliar ring.

etheric_storm.line: You shelter against a tilted column as the storm rolls over. Blue and purple lightning sheets the plain. The strange pressure climbs.
A bolt strikes a few paces from you — the old bedrock in the soil holds the charge, and a hand-sized shard of stormglass crystallises around the impact.
etheric_storm.arbiterLine: "That does not happen for everyone," the {narrator} says.

effects.text: An Etheric storm gave you a fragment instead of killing you. That counts for something here.

pulsing_mud.line: You step toward the glow. The mud is warm against your boot — an old bedrock deposit, surface-thin but real.
You pry the deposit out of the dirt. A few good shards, dense and humming, plus a thumb-sized core.

frozen_statue.line: You circle the figure. An old functionary by the cut of their robes, perfectly preserved inside a casing of strange hardened glass — even their satchel still hangs from the shoulder.
You chip the satchel free without disturbing the body. Inside: a sealed scroll case and a small purse of pre-flood coin.
frozen_statue.arbiterLine: "Treat them like the dead," the {narrator} says. "Not the museum piece."

effects.text: You took a satchel off a body the mud preserved at the moment of the flood.

sentinel_patrol.line: You lay flat and watch. The construct runs a perfect loop — twelve paces east, pause, twelve paces back. Old programming, never updated.
You time the loop and slip across its blind arc. Whatever it was guarding is past the wall — and unguarded for as long as you are quiet.

effects.text: You crossed a Sentinel patrol unseen. You know its blind arc now.

mud_golem_stir.line: You back off to the treeline and watch. The mud reforms itself — slow, deliberate — into a hulking shape of stone and dirt. It does not see you yet.
The Golem turns toward your scent. It has decided.
mud_golem_stir.arbiterLine: "Aether Golems do not negotiate," the {narrator} says.

temporal_eddy.line: You step into the shimmer. Your shadow falls in three directions at once, then snaps back.
Hours pass in what felt like a step — and a single clear thought lands in your head that wasn't there before. A name and a place. The eddy paid in directions.
temporal_eddy.arbiterLine: "The Aetheric eddies sometimes pay in knowledge instead of coin," the {narrator} says. "Check your contracts board — the eddy added one."

spatial_warp.line: You step forward. Twenty paces become three. The world is being economical with you.
You come out of the fold a long way from where you started — but on higher ground, with a view of a structure you weren't aware was here.

effects.text: A spatial warp shortcut you to ground you would not have found on foot.

spatial_warp.line: The new vantage clears your head. You knew This country bent space — now you know what it feels like.

whisper_crystal.line: You lean toward the crystal. The whispering shapes itself — old, you think, though no language you can name. It is saying a location.
You pry the crystal loose. The whispering stops — but the direction it gave you stays.

effects.text: A whisper-crystal told you where a sealed vault is. You haven't found it yet.

whisper_crystal.line: You stand at the place the crystal indicated. The whispering crystal in your pack warms once and goes still.

black_cloak.line: You double back through a fold in the ground. The Black Cloak passes you, scanning the path you should have been on, and does not see you.
black_cloak.arbiterLine: "Mud Monarch enforcement," the {narrator} says quietly. "Do not let them see what you carry."

black_cloak.line: When the Cloak is past, you check what they dropped — a sealed dispatch slip, smudged with strange ink. Worth something, to the right buyer.

effects.text: You lifted a Mud Monarch dispatch off a Black Cloak. The Order will pay for it.

giant_silhouette.line: You make your way to where the figure stood. The ground is pressed — a foot print, far larger than any human boot, and the air still smells faintly of ozone.
A single object sits where the print is deepest — a carved stone token, mark of a watching elder. Lore says a Giant leaves these for the few they decide to remember.
giant_silhouette.arbiterLine: "Sasquatch, Yeti, Bigfoot — every age gives them a different name," the {narrator} says. "They are watching you. Try to be worth it."

effects.text: A Tartarian Giant left you a token. You are being watched.

bioluminescent_path.line: You follow the fungi. The trail leads down through a slumped wall into a low chamber — a True old way-station, currently unstaffed, but lived-in.
A bowl of mud-stew, still warm. A folded cot. A sigil scratched into the doorway — passage granted. You take only what is offered, and leave.
bioluminescent_path.arbiterLine: "You showed restraint," the {narrator} says. "They will know."

wreck_construct.line: You crouch over the construct. Its arm still moves, but the core flickers — a few more hours, then nothing. Salvage now or never.
You pry the core free and strip the workable plating. A scavenger would weep at this haul.

submerged_steeple.line: You wade out to the steeple. The window-slits at the top open onto a flooded nave — old bedrock shimmer in the water below.
submerged_steeple.arbiterLine: "Explorers have gone in," the {narrator} says, "and the water keeps them."

submerged_steeple.line: You dive. The old bedrock gives you a half-minute of breathable air. You grab what you can — a heavy reliquary off the altar — and break back to the surface, lungs burning.

effects.text: You dove the Sinking Cathedral and came back up. Most don't.

black_market_lantern.line: You duck through the culvert. A small market — three stalls, no chatter, eyes on you immediately. They will trade. They will not trust you.
You haggle into a fair price for a single item — marsh-folk stock you do not usually see above ground.

effects.text: A hidden Mud Dweller market sold you a piece of Tartarian stealth kit.

aether_grid_hum.line: You follow the grid line east. The hum strengthens. You crest a low rise and look down at an old node — half-buried, partially active.
You touch the node. It accepts you — or doesn't see you as a threat, which here is close enough. A small charge runs through your pack: every strange thing you carry is faintly steadier now.
aether_grid_hum.arbiterLine: "That is older than every faction," the {narrator} says. "It does not have politics."

effects.text: You found a still-warm Aetheric grid node. It did not reject you.

sealed_vault_door.line: You scrape the mud off the locking ring. The glyphs are an old tumbler — three rotations, in the right order. The faint markings tell you which.
The door grinds inward. Inside: a small storeroom, every shelf still loaded. Whoever sealed this expected to come back.

effects.text: You opened a sealed Tartarian vault. Whoever sealed it is centuries late.

preserved_corpse.line: You kneel beside the body. The hardened glass froze them mid-fall — robes intact, satchel intact. The seal on the satchel is old orders.
You take the satchel — they would have wanted a scholar to have it. Inside: a research scroll, a small purse, and a runecaster casing.
preserved_corpse.arbiterLine: "The Order will know you took it from one of theirs," the {narrator} says. "They will count that in your favour."

effects.text: You recovered a Forgotten Order satchel from a preserved corpse.

loose_floorboard.line: You work the board up. Beneath it, a shallow void packed with oilcloth — a hidden stash, undisturbed since whoever stowed it stopped coming back.
Inside the oilcloth: a fistful of old coin and a coil of salvageable wire.
loose_floorboard.arbiterLine: "The buried world keeps its secrets under the floor as often as under the mud," the {narrator} says.

hidden_compartment.line: You press the panel and it gives with a soft click, swinging back on a hidden hinge.
Folded in the cavity: a strip of cured cloth and a few coins someone meant to come back for.

watching_portrait.line: You lift the portrait off its hook. The wall behind it is bare but for a single line of old script, scratched into the plaster by hand.
The script is a name and a warning: do not answer if it knocks from inside. You copy it into memory — it may matter later.
watching_portrait.arbiterLine: "Someone was afraid of this house," the {narrator} notes. "Or of what they kept in it."

effects.text: A scratched warning behind a portrait: "do not answer if it knocks from inside."

bricked_doorway.line: You knock a few loose bricks free. The mortar is newer than the wall — and behind it, cold air moves. The sealed room still breathes.
You widen the gap and reach through. A storeroom, long shut — your hand closes on a coil of patched cloth and a heavy old coin.

bloodstain_rug.line: You pull the rug back. The stain runs to a loose seam in the boards — and a small bundle wedged into the gap beneath, hidden in haste.
Inside the bundle, wrapped against the damp: a salvage of metal and a handful of coin. Whoever bled here was trying to hide this first.

open_ledger.line: You read down the ledger. The struck-through names share a column heading you recognise — a debt-list, and the unstruck names are still owed.
The last wet entry names a place you can find. You commit it to memory; a lead like this pays out later.
open_ledger.arbiterLine: "Names and numbers," the {narrator} murmurs. "The most dangerous lore there is."

effects.text: A debt-ledger named an unsettled account — a lead worth following.

childs_drawing.line: You take the drawing down. On the back, in the same crayon, a single shaky word: HOME — with an arrow, pointing down.
A child drew what they saw, and what they saw was true. The image stays with you — the buried world remembers its giants, even through a child.

effects.text: A child's drawing of a giant figure, marked HOME with an arrow pointing down.

stopped_clock.line: You open the clock case. The mechanism is whole — no broken spring, no jam. It simply stopped, all at once, the way clocks do where the strangeness ran wild.
Tucked behind the face, a thin disc of Aether-glass, still faintly warm. You pry it loose.

scratched_door.line: You crouch to the marks. Worn into the wood below them, almost smooth, is a knot you can press — a catch, hidden where a trapped hand would have found it last.
The catch releases a narrow drawer in the door frame. Inside: a few coins and a scrap of cloth, a prisoner's last cache.

warm_chair.line: You set a hand on the seat. Still warm — but the room is empty, the dust unbroken. Whatever rose from this chair left no tracks at all.
Down the side of the cushion your fingers find what was left behind — a few coins, still warm from a body that is no longer here. You take them and do not look back.
warm_chair.arbiterLine: "Don't wait for the host," the {narrator} says. "This one doesn't keep to the hours of the living."

crooked_shelf.line: You pull at the mismatched shelf. It swings outward on a concealed pivot — behind it, a crawlspace, barely wide enough, breathing cold.
The crawlspace ends in a niche someone used as a strongroom — patched cloth, scrap, and coin, left when the house was abandoned.

ceiling_drip.line: You climb to the wet spot. Above the boards, a void — and something resting in it that the water has been running off for years.
You bring it down: a sealed Tartarian canister, its seam still good, salvage rattling inside.

bolted_strongbox.line: You work the tumbler. It is old and stiff, but the glyphs warm under your hand, and on the third try the bolt draws back.
The strongbox holds what a careful household saves for a bad year: coin, and metal worth more than coin.

aether_tang.line: You follow the taste to its source — a hairline crack in the wall, and behind it a thread of the strangeness-glass laid into the house's bones, still live.
You ease a length of the glass free. It hums faintly in your palm before it dims — raw Aether residue, the good kind.

barefoot_prints.line: You follow the prints to where they stop. The dust there is pressed flat in a circle — something stood here a long while, then was simply gone.
In the centre of the circle, set down as if placed, lies a small coin-purse. You take it. The house holds its breath; you let it.
barefoot_prints.arbiterLine: "Take it and go," the {narrator} says, very quietly. "Some debts you do not want to be present to collect."
